beats.care: Going out with a younger sibling or grandparent? Save your number on them, and approach the nearest cop if anyone goes missing.
beats.what: Ten police vans, each with a woman constable and a volunteer, are patrolling pandals from Panchami to Dashami, into the early hours.
beats.why: Children and elderly people are most likely to get separated in dense Puja crowds.

opts: Tell the nearest police person right away
cards.q: If your little cousin gets lost at a pandal, what's the quickest first step?
cards.why: Police say to reach the nearest officer; a report gets shared with every station in the city.

cards.body: Each van carries a sub-inspector or ASI, a constable, a woman constable and a volunteer. Found children are taken to the nearest police station and looked after by women officers.
cards.title: What's in the van

cards.body: The crews carry balloons, chips and chocolates to calm lost kids.

cards.q: Does your group have a 'lost' meeting spot?

hook: What should you do if someone in your group *gets lost* at a pandal?

learn.t: A missing-child report at one pandal is passed to the local police station, which alerts every other station in the city.

sources.name: The Statesman
sources.title: Lost while pandal-hopping? Kolkata Police launch initiative to reunite families this Durga Puja

sources.name: Asianet Newsable
sources.title: Durga Puja 2026: Kolkata Police Introduce New App To Trace Missing Persons During Pandal Hopping

tldr: Kolkata Police have put 10 'Bondhu Kolkata' vans on the streets till Dashami to find kids and elders who get separated from family in Puja crowds.
